correctness.rationale: The n+1 candidate insertions form a tree with one edge per deletion position and connected consecutive edges. Odd-syndrome vertices yield a symmetric-difference representation of the check support as intervals, forcing at least r odd parents. Compatible boundary-bit assignments yield r exactly in the stated regimes, with syndrome of first designated parent congruent to r-1+sum(ell_j*t_j)=1. For one even run a sole odd parent would have even syndrome, and an explicit witness has two. The Fibonacci bound uses unique tilings by 0 and 11. Actual verifier enumerated each deletion parent list for 1012 hyperplanes through length nine and replayed 32230 witness constructions.

originality.rationale: The precise run-bound, its equality conditions for arbitrarily located parity-check masks, and exponential prevalence were compared against the source paper, related edit-distance literature, accessible historical claims and targeted published-finding corpus searches. The originating paper proves only the alternating-mask counterexample as part of a more general list-rate bound; that special case does not imply the all-mask support-run statement. Closest available published-finding corpus items describe different channels. Unindexed equivalent results remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or older theorem about Fourier coefficients of deletion insertion balls or interval incidence colorings may imply this result implicitly.
Full texts of older edit-distance references were not reviewed exhaustively; their abstracts concern different invariants.
The unclassified odd-run-count/all-even-run subclass is deliberately left with only an upper bound.

value.rationale: The binary exception in a newly published generalized half-Singleton paper motivates understanding which coordinate patterns of a high-rate binary linear check admit small single-deletion candidate lists. This work provides a sharp structural parameter (number of check support runs), proves equality for nearly all masks with an explicit constructed received word, identifies a genuine parity obstruction for a lone even run, and bounds the unclassified population by Fibonacci growth, exponentially negligible among the 2^n masks. This is not an isolated small computation or a renaming of the known alternating-mask example.
